Here are the findings from `app.log` (72,324 lines, 02:00–04:00 UTC on 2026-01-18):

### (1) First real error burst — time & host

The **first actual error** was on **api-07** at **`T03:17:42Z`**:
```
ERROR api-07 db pool exhausted (max=20) waiting=14 path=/v1/orders
```
Within seconds, the error cascade hit **all hosts** (api-01 through api-08), producing hundreds of `503 upstream=db pool exhausted` errors per second across the cluster.

*(Earlier at T02:41:07Z there was a single isolated TLS handshake failure on api-02 — unrelated noise, not part of the outage.)*

### (2) Root cause

**DB connection pool exhaustion.** The pool had `max=20` connections and all 20 were held open by a long-running batch job that never released them. Meanwhile normal API traffic on the same pool kept arriving, hitting `waiting=14` requests and starting to time out with 503s once the pool was saturated.

### (3) Responsible batch/job/user

**Host `batch-01`** ran the **`reconcile-ledger`** job as user **`svc-batch`**:
- Started at **`T03:15:03Z`** with `db_conns=20` (grabbed all 20 connections from the pool)
- Acquired them one-by-one over ~24 seconds until pool was drained to 0/20
- Did not release any connections

The job finally finished at **`T03:41:30Z`** (`rows=48210112`, `released_conns=20`), after which errors stopped. The outage window was roughly **03:17–03:41 UTC (~24 minutes)**.
